subject: [PATCH v3 01/11] mm, swap: add virtual swap device infrastructure

reviews.author: Nhat Pham (author)
reviews.summary:
Author acknowledges that the reviewer's suggestions are sensible and has already implemented most of them, plans to continue testing before reporting back.

Author addressed concerns about CONFIG_VSWAP by removing it, replacing the runtime parameter with a boot parameter, and adding logic to handle 32-bit systems. They plan to test for potential bugs before proceeding.

The author acknowledged a concern about the renaming of the swap_info_struct field and agreed to remove the cluster_reclaim_range() code path for vswap clusters, as it is not triggered in their benchmarks.

Author agrees to rename vswap_alloc_cluster to vswap_alloc_swap_entry, but is hesitant to introduce new surface for linking newly allocated clusters to the free list and may mess up handling when unlinking them.

The author acknowledged that they tend to forget about certain flags and agreed to add them, indicating that the patch will need further revision.
reviews.raw_body:
On Fri, Aug 7, 2026 at 8:49 AM Johannes Weiner <hannes@cmpxchg.org> wrote:

Hi Johannes,

My apologies for the delayed response. I saw and read your email, but
I wanted to stew on it, code things out, and stare at things before
responding.

I think most of our suggestions here make sense. I coded most of them
out already, and I'm stress testing them - will report back if there
are surprises.

---

I've been thinking about this and your other suggestions regarding
removing CONFIG_VSWAP. I've coded them out - it does indeed look
cleaner :)

Let me test things first to make sure I did not introduce some weird
bugs, but to recap:

1. CONFIG_VSWAP gone (along with most of the !CONFIG_VSWAP stubs,
saving 100 LoCs or so).

2. Runtime param gone, replaced by a boot param.

3. CONFIG_VSWAP_DEFAULT_ENABLED only decides the default value of the
boot param (still gated by 64bit config).

4. If we detect that the system is 32 bit, we ignore bootparam
selection by users (with a small warn).

If the boot param is false (either because of user selection, the
build config, or because the system is 32 bit), we don't allocate the
vswap device, and bypass all vswap code paths. There should be
negligible overhead here.

---

Good point in the renaming, yeah.

On a related note, I'm thinking of just removing this piece of code in
cluster_reclaim_range(). We have no signal to trigger
cluster_reclaim_range() (i.e swap-cache-only reclamation) for vswap
clusters, and vswap (similar to swap-sync-io devices such as zram)
already try to free swap slots (and swap cache) when the last PTE
reference of the swap entry is dropped. I don't think this code path
is triggered at all in my benchmarks.

Let's keep cluster_reclaim_range() for phys swap device only.

---

That name was vestigial from Kairui's RFC, but yeah I agree
vswap_alloc_cluster sounds better.

Regarding the linkage of the newly allocated cluster to the free list
- I'm a bit hesitant to introduce new surface for these clusters,
mostly because I'm afraid I might mess up the handling of these
clusters (when I unlink them from the free list), but I can give it a
shot.

---

Will do yeah. I tend to forget them myself too :) SWP_SOLIDSTATE is
mostly to opt-in to the cluster-based allocaiton algo. SWP_WRITEOK is
checked in a couple of places to allow allocation.

2026-08-18.patch_summary: This patch introduces the infrastructure for a virtual swap device, allowing for dynamic allocation of swap space. It creates a 16 TB virtual swap device at boot and sets up the necessary data structures to manage it. The patch also adds support for the SWP_VSWAP flag, which allows hot paths to skip per-device bookkeeping that doesn't apply to virtual swap devices. This is the first in a series of patches that will enable the use of virtual swap devices, including backends and vswap-aware swap-out and swap-in paths.

reviews.author: Nhat Pham (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed a concern about the swap allocator's behavior in the virtual swap case, explaining that the new code is intended to put newly allocated clusters on the free list and then have vswap scan it for allocation. They acknowledged potential lock contention issues but decided to rename alloc_swap_scan_dynamic() to vswap_cluster_alloc() as a temporary fix.

2026-08-19.patch_summary: This patch introduces the infrastructure for a virtual swap device, allowing for dynamic allocation of swap space. It creates a 16 TB virtual swap device at boot and sets up the necessary data structures to manage it. The patch also adds support for the SWP_VSWAP flag, which allows hot paths to skip per-device bookkeeping that doesn't apply to virtual swap devices. This is the first in a series of patches that will enable the use of virtual swap devices, including backends and vswap-aware swap-out and swap-in paths.
